title: Split streaming assembler into lightweight stages and add KV liveness probes
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Background: The streaming request assembler currently operates as a monolithic stage that performs request coalescing, prefetch coordination, and KV cache touches on the same thread. This design simplifies the code paths but causes CPU stalling and unpredictable tail latency during GC/eviction storms. Objective: Decompose the streaming assembler into three lightweight stages (ingest, coalesce/dispatch, and kv-touch worker) connected by bounded handoff queues, and introduce an explicit KV liveness probe + small API for checking k-v shard freshness. Goals: reduce 99.9th token latency by 15-25% under sustained load, cut CPU spikes during large cache migrations, and surface clear telemetry for cache staleness that the scheduler can use to make routing decisions.

Proposed implementation:
- Create a Streaming Ingest stage that normalizes and timestamps incoming requests, performs early validation, and forwards minimal descriptors to the coalescer.
- Implement a Coalesce/Dispatch stage that groups request descriptors into micro-batches and decides whether the batch should be executed locally or routed to a warm shard.
- Add KV-touch worker(s) that perform only KV reads/warmups as idempotent async tasks; these run on a separate threadpool and expose a small liveness API (kv_shard_last_touch_ns and kv_shard_staleness_hint) that the scheduler can query.
- Introduce bounded queue lengths and backpressure hooks so the ingest stage applies soft drops when the kv-touch pool is saturated; the drop policy is configurable by tenant.
- Add unit + integration tests for ordering and correctness guarantees; add a canary regression suite using our perf harness to compare latency and throughput across variants.

Compatibility and migration:
- The new KV liveness API is additive and backward compatible; scheduler fallbacks will continue to work against the old contract until rollout completes.
- We'll implement a feature flag (stream-assembler-split-v2) to gate runtime activation per region/cluster.

Observability and rollout:
- Emit new metrics: kv_shard_last_touch_ns, kv_shard_staleness_hint, assembler_queue_depth_{ingest,coalesce,kv}, assembler_stage_latency_{p50,p95,p99,p999}.
- Dashboards: create "Assembler Stages" tab linked in the runtime-ops Grafana group.
- Rollout strategy: canary on staging -> canary in dedicated-us-west -> gradual 25% ramp across regions with automated SLO gates (p999 latency and error rate) and automatic rollback on SLO regression.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Production canary shows p999 token latency improvement >= 10% with no increase in error rate.
2) KV liveness metrics surface useful signals and correlate with observed cache misses in the heatmap.
3) No correctness regressions; all ordering/in-flight tests pass.
4) Documented migration and feature flag exercised during rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: introducing bounded queues could increase request drops under pathological bursts. Mitigation: soft-drop policy + per-tenant thresholds and immediate fallback to cold model variant.
- Risk: KV-touch async pool contention. Mitigation: adaptive pool sizing and preflight warmup for heavy tenants.
